findings.text: Two small leftovers. README.md:193 still lists an echoed `{name}` in headings and titles, though the heading no longer has one and only the field value echoes it. Separately, a neighbour who goes Back after reserving and whose browser re-fetches GET /reserve/<id> sees M3, 'just taken', on their own book, because a GET carries no token. The design calls for M3 when the form is opened on a reserved book, and A9's mechanism covers POST repeats, so this conforms. It is still the nearest remaining edge of A9's stated aim.

debt.drag: The stale phrase may mislead page-access; the Back path is an unwitnessed edge of A9's stated aim.

reasons: A1 met: Reserve links carry a visually hidden title, held books have none, and the form follows the design (T-4 test, src/pages.js bookItem and formPage).
A2 met: the confirmation names the book, address and hold end, worded from the stored reservedUntil, with no name (T-20 test and the settings test).
A3 met: one visible field plus the hidden token; the confirmation's only exit is the link back to the shelf (T-28 test).
A4 met: 409 M3 with a link back; bytes, inode and mtime are unchanged (T-6 test).
A5 met: blank, whitespace-only and format-only names get 400 and the same book's form, with nothing written (T-7 test).
A6 met: the check and write sit together inside updateShelf; twenty real HTTP POSTs give one 303 and nineteen 409, and the file holds the winner's name (T-32 test).

A7 met: createApp takes a now option read per request, the exact end still holds, end+1ms frees the book and it can be reserved again; T-18 and T-2 are asserted on the new pages, and the default clock is tested.

A8 met: 404 M2, 503 M6 with Retry-After, the 60-code-point limit, control characters refused, esc on every page, and 413 for both declared and chunked oversize bodies. Non-busy write failures are noted separately.
A9 met: the POST answers 303; a same-token repeat redirects with no write, including concurrently; a different token gets M3.
Non-goals respected: no settings file read, no client-side script, no search, no accounts. Touching store.js for heldEnd serves the intent and the spec records it (store-heldEnd-export).
The redaction path holds: names and claims are absent from pages and logs, and Refusal carries none. The persistence path holds: refusals throw before the save.
UI was reviewed from markup and CSS against the design record; no browser was available here, so nothing was rendered, and the tap-target, contrast and 360px rules were not measured.
The lane ledger shows no lanes; the executable checks report all 19 witnesses present and all mutation-smoke targets killed. My local `node --test test/` passed 68 of 68, on Node v26.13.0.

premises.claim: updateShelf saves unless change throws, so refusals by throw write nothing.
isHeld keeps a book with a missing or unreadable end held, and heldEnd is what keeps such a book from getting a confirmation.
